title: Depend on GitDiffKit 0.2.0 and require macOS 26 (step 2.9)
body:
Step 2.9 of the split plan, the tools part: swift-steward moves to [GitDiffKit 0.2.0](https://github.com/marosoaie/git-diff-parser/releases/tag/0.2.0), the release with the layered diff model (event parser, `DiffSummary`, the full `Diff`) that Steward needs from Phase 4 on.

## What changed

- **Dependency.** `Package.swift` depends on `git-diff-parser` `from: "0.2.0"`. `Package.resolved` pins `0.2.0` at `ff1a045`, and no other pin moved.
- **Platforms: macOS 14 → 26.** The library needs the 26 releases on Apple platforms because its API uses `Span` (design decision Q7). Linux has no floor. The manifest now says why, so the floor doesn't get lowered by mistake. The release binary now declares `minos 26.0` (v2.0.0 declares 14.0).
- **The library's breaking changes.** Only one reaches this package: `DiffParser.consume(_: Data)` is gone, because the library no longer imports Foundation. The CLI's streaming reader (`Sources/StewardCLI/InputOutput.swift`) and the real-world test helper now pass `[UInt8](data)`. That's the same copy 0.1.0 made inside `consume(_: Data)`, so the cost is unchanged. `BuildLogKit`'s own `consume(_: Data)` stays.
- **README.** The build-from-source floor (macOS 26+), the library snippet (`from: "0.2.0"`), and the chunk types `DiffParser.consume` accepts.

No version bump: `CommandConfiguration.version` stays `2.0.0`, and the maintainer picks the next one. Dropping macOS 14 and 15 may be worth weighing when picking it.

## Merge order with the tap

The next release built from this commit runs only on macOS 26. **Draft [homebrew-tap#3](https://github.com/marosoaie/homebrew-tap/pull/3) adds the matching `depends_on macos: :tahoe` (inside `on_macos`) to the `steward` formula. It merges right before the next Release run**, not earlier: until then the formula pins v2.0.0, which runs on macOS 14. The Release workflow's re-pin `sed` only touches `tag:` and `revision:`, so it works with the new line. This PR can merge on its own schedule; nothing ships until Release runs.

## Tests run

macOS 26.6.2 (Apple Silicon), Xcode 27.0, Swift 6.4. Unless noted, on `ee0f542`; `a9fab34` only adds the manifest comment and was re-tested with `swift build --build-tests`, `swift test` and SwiftLint.

| Command | Inputs | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `swift build --build-tests`, `swift build -c release` | full rebuild (the deployment target changed) | Build complete, **0 warnings** |
| `swift test --enable-code-coverage` (network tests on) | cached kernel, redis and swift-argument-parser fixtures | **48 tests in 12 suites + 74 tests in 13 suites passed**, the same as `main` (the GitHub API's opt-in live suites skip, as on `main`) |
| `swift test` on `a9fab34` | same | 48 + 74 passed |
| `xcodebuild test -scheme swift-steward-Package -destination platform=macOS` | – | **TEST SUCCEEDED**, 48 + 74; no compiler warnings |
| `swiftlint lint --quiet` | whole tree | prints nothing |
| Linux: `swift build --build-tests -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors && swift test --skip-build` in `swift:6.2` (6.2.4, aarch64, Colima) | committed tree, cached fixtures | build clean, **122 tests in 25 suites passed** |
| `swift test --package-path Tooling` | – | 26 tests in 4 suites passed |
| `Tooling/check-github-api-drift.sh` (drift guard) | pinned spec | "The committed GitHub client matches the pipeline's output"; tree clean |
| Coverage: `llvm-cov` export, hand-written `Sources/` (excluding `Generated/`) | – | **507/544 (93.2%), unchanged from `main`** (507/544). The ruleset's 70% rule reads uploaded Cobertura reports only, and none is uploaded yet (see `docs/github-api.md`) |

### End to end: output byte-identical to v2.0.0

Three release binaries, run on the same 263 cases. For every case, stdout, stderr and the exit code are compared with `cmp`:
- `v2.0.0`: brew's `steward` 2.0.0.
- `main`: built from `main` at `3b9df8f` before this change.
- `new`: built from this branch.

Inputs:
- **Diffs:** Linux 6.6→6.7 (70 MB), redis 7.0.0→7.2.0, swift-argument-parser 1.0.0→1.5.0, the swift PR #70000 fixture, and the unit Sonar diff.
- **Logs:** the test fixtures' xcodebuild, SwiftLint and SwiftFormat logs and Sonar JSON. Also step 1.4's real logs: swift-argument-parser 1.5.0 under `xcodebuild build`, `swift build`, `swiftlint lint` (2,127 warnings, 349 errors) and `swiftformat --lint` (25,643 diagnostics); redis 7.2.0 under `clang -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra` (1,003 warnings); and a 2,476-issue Sonar report.

Cases:
- **`changes`:** 25 cases (json and text, from a file and from stdin, on every diff).
- **`filter`:** 219 cases (every log × each tool that applies × json/github/text, plus `--fail-on` note/warning/error, `--tolerance` 3 and 50, `--repo-root`, log from stdin, diff from stdin, and logs against unrelated diffs).
- **Errors and help:** 19 cases (missing files and arguments, bad option values, an unknown subcommand, `--version`, help).

| Comparison | Result |
|---|---|
| `v2.0.0` vs `new` | **263/263 cases identical (789/789 files)** |
| `main` vs `new` | 263/263 identical |
| `v2.0.0` vs `main` (baseline sanity) | 263/263 identical |
| `v2.0.0` vs a `brew install --build-from-source` of this commit (below) | 263/263 identical |

The tests' own pinned fingerprints (`CommandLineOutputTests`) also pass on macOS and Linux.

**Probes for the library's documented behavior changes** (CHANGELOG, "Changed"), with `changes` json and text, v2.0.0 vs new:
- Identical: `git log -p -300` of this repo (1.8 MB) and of git-diff-parser (1.0 MB), where paths come up again further down the stream. Also a real merge's combined diffs (`git show --cc`, `git show -c`, `git log -p --cc`), which both skip, and its `--diff-merges=first-parent` diff.
- Different, as the CHANGELOG says: a hand-made diff with a lone `+++ lone` line between two hunks. v2.0.0 invented a file `lone`; 0.2.0 no longer starts a file at a lone `+++`. git never writes this, so output can change only on damaged input.

### Benchmark (release builds, `/usr/bin/time -l`; v2.0.0 and new in two alternating rounds, main once before the change)

| Case | v2.0.0 | main | new |
|---|---|---|---|
| `changes` kernel 6.6→6.7 (70 MB), 5 runs, median | 0.20 s, 68 MB | 0.21 s, 67 MB | **0.19 s, 68 MB** |
| `changes -` 6× kernel via stdin (422 MB), 3 runs, median | 0.77 s, 68 MB | 0.77 s, 67 MB | **0.67 s, 68 MB** |
| `filter` swiftformat log (7.9 MB) vs the kernel diff, 3 runs, median | 2.67 s, 43 MB | 2.68 s, 43 MB | **2.64 s, 43 MB** |

Within the ~0.2 s / 70 MB budget, with flat peak memory.

### The formula (for [homebrew-tap#3](https://github.com/marosoaie/homebrew-tap/pull/3))

The tap PR's formula was tested as a keg-only scratch copy (`steward-check`) that builds this commit from a local clone:
- `brew install --build-from-source` succeeded (32 s).
- `brew test` passed.
- The installed binary declares `minos 26.0`, and its output is 263/263 identical to v2.0.0's.
- `brew style` and `brew audit --strict --online` pass on the tap's formula.
- `brew info --variations` lists the macOS requirement for macOS only.

The installed `steward` 2.0.0 and the brew trust list were left untouched.

## Review

`codex review --base origin/main` (model `gpt-6.1-sol`, stdin closed) on `ee0f542`: **0 findings**. In its words: "The dependency bump, platform requirement, and streaming API conversions are consistent." Its sandbox kept it from building; the suites above ran outside it. After the review, `a9fab34` added only the two-line manifest comment on the floor.
